To Ireland

, contained the kind of extreme passionate nationalism that Joyce seems to be lampooning in this parody. Robert Emmet, whose public funeral the parody supposedly describes, was executed in 1803, eighteen years prior to Lady Jane’s birth. There was, in fact, no public funeral for Emmet. Joyce was wary of such excessive emotionalism would devolve into kitsch.
